- [ASSISTANT_SAID] There can be sub-architecture types within each of the main architecture types.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Within the native desktop application architecture type, there could be subtypes like single-page applications, event-driven applications, or multithreaded applications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Within the cross-platform desktop application architecture type, there could be subtypes like containerization, virtualization, or cloud-native applications.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The same applies to web-based desktop and hybrid desktop application architectures, with subtypes that can include progressive web applications (PWA), single-page applications (SPA), or responsive web design (RWD) among others.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The choice of sub-architecture type will depend on the specific requirements of the project and the development team's expertise.
- [USER] Please update the list so that pros and cons are listed for all sub-architecture types.
- [USER] Currently, the table is missing this information for "C# or .NET", "JavaFX", "Single Page Applications", and "Electron with web view".
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Here's an updated table with the missing pros and cons for various architecture types.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] A table with the following structure:
  - Architecture Type: Native Desktop Application
  - Sub-Architecture Types: C++ or MFC, C# or .NET, Java Swing, WinForms, WPF
  - Pros: Can offer good performance and integration with the operating system's features.
  - Cons: Can be more complex and time-consuming to develop, and may require different versions for different operating systems.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] A table with the following structure:
  - Architecture Type: Cross-Platform Desktop App
  - Sub-Architecture Types: Electron, Qt, JavaFX, .NET Core
  - Pros: Can save time and resources by using a single codebase for multiple operating systems.
  - Cons: May not offer the same level of performance or integration with the operating system's features as a native desktop application.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] A table with the following structure:
  - Architecture Type: Web-Based Desktop Application
  - Sub-Architecture Types: Single Page Applications (SPA), Progressive Web Apps (PWA), WebViews, Frameworks
  - Pros: Can be relatively easy to develop and deploy, and can offer good compatibility across different operating systems.
  - Cons: May not offer the same level of performance or integration with the operating system's features as a native desktop application.
